runtime.note: The screenshots show the published 3.46.2 runtime, not the 3.46.3 source tree.

environment.desktop: Debian/Xfce in a task-owned Docker virtual computer

method.source: Gdk root framebuffer captured through the ai-computer virtual desktop
method.postProcessing: None; no compositing, synthetic UI, cropping or pixel edits.
method.verification: All 18 public screenshots were visually reviewed. Dimensions were read from each PNG header. Repository SHA-256 hashes match the corresponding container captures. UTC timestamps come from the latest matching filename entries in the append-only capture log. Private recording hashes were independently checked from the host copies.
method.operator: Agent-operated real software, with operator review and approval steps; not an independent human usability study.
method.privacyReview: No credential values were visible in the 18 reviewed public PNGs. This manifest does not claim a full-frame privacy review of the private raw recordings.

narrative.meaning: Three compressed demonstration sessions on 2026-10-11, not three elapsed days.
limits: The captures are selected real UI states, not a continuous reliability test.
Maya's memory suggestions were reviewed and accepted by the operator.
Invitations remained drafts and no purchases were made.
Provider cost is not established by these screenshots; a zero cost field must not be interpreted as free usage.

The saved goal completed after four work sessions across the three compressed demonstration sessions. Some original description and next-step wording remained stale; the completion badge and progress summary are recorded accurately.

recordings.note: The main recording begins after the initial package installation. The second recording captures a genuine separate installation into a new prefix and fresh data directory, with existing download cache available.

files.content: Supplemental second installation, launch recovery and fresh app home page.

files.hashVerification: SHA-256 independently verified from the private host copy

screenshots.caption: A terminal receipt shows flujo-ai 3.46.2 installed with 551 packages in 55 seconds and the fresh instance ready at localhost:4300.
notes: Supplemental second installation. The terminal re-displays the actual npm log, npm ls result and ready URL after completion. The command ran in a previously absent prefix using the existing npm download cache. See installationEvidence for the measured time and port-conflict recovery.

screenshots.caption: The newly installed second instance opens its fresh home page at localhost:4300.
notes: Supplemental second installation with a new package prefix and fresh FLUJO data. This later capture followed dismissal of a transient toast and does not replace the original main-journey home capture.

screenshots.caption: FLUJO's home page at localhost:4200 after the published package had been installed.
notes: Shows the running app and setup entry point; it does not show or prove the installation command.

screenshots.caption: Workshop AI passes the provider, adapter and FLUJO tool round-trip tests.
notes: OpenRouter model google/gemini-3-flash-preview. The displayed 1,718 ms, 1,117 ms and 3,184 ms values are this test's measured durations, not estimates or performance guarantees. This successful capture replaces an earlier failed provider-test screenshot.

screenshots.caption: The GitHub import form accepts zcaceres/fetch-mcp and offers Clone repository.
notes: The valid-repository result and local destination are visible; this frame precedes cloning.

screenshots.caption: The cloned fetch-mcp server passes its MCP handshake and exposes six tools.
notes: Visible install command: npm install --include=dev. Visible build command: npm run build. The connection log shows node dist/index.js; the run-configuration section is collapsed.

screenshots.caption: The saved fetch-mcp configuration uses Standard IO with command node and argument dist/index.js.
notes: Supplementary later capture: the saved server was reopened in Edit, the run-configuration section expanded, then the dialog canceled without changes.

screenshots.caption: Coffee workshop helper is saved with Workshop AI and the fetch-mcp app.
notes: The app binding includes all six tools. This is not evidence that only fetch_readable was granted.

screenshots.caption: The helper returns a corrected eight-bullet checklist, separating source advice from workshop planning choices.
notes: This is the corrected result after asking for the complete source with fetch_readable max_length 20000. The earlier 5,000-character extract omitted the brewing steps and led to an incorrect ratio. The frame is not a claim of a correct first reply.

screenshots.caption: Maya's creation review shows the Workshop planner role, Workshop AI, fetch-mcp and two required behaviors.
notes: The wizard says Ready to create and memory starts empty; this frame precedes clicking Create Persona.

screenshots.caption: The Day 1 goal form contains its title, context, ongoing-work option and final-approval success criteria.
notes: Later setup-form retake after the real goal completed: the original inputs were re-entered to show the fully filled form. Start working is enabled, but the dialog was canceled and no duplicate goal was created. The completed goal remains visible behind the dialog.

screenshots.caption: Maya's invitation draft is remembered while the initial workshop-plan suggestion still needs review.
notes: The screenshot records the review process between two acceptance actions. It does not show both suggestions accepted. The remembered card still contains stale explanatory wording saying it awaits review.

screenshots.caption: Maya's first goal response shows a 90-minute plan for six adults at three shared stations and the beginning of an invitation draft.
notes: The screenshot shows the initial plan and invitation heading; the invitation continues below the visible area.

screenshots.caption: Maya's Day 2 shopping list gives regular and decaf coffee, filter, water and equipment quantities.
notes: Later capture of the persisted Day 2 chat response. This intermediate list includes four equipment sets and 20+ cups; the final reviewed pack makes the fourth lead set optional and records 24 cups. The quantities are planning estimates, not quantities specified by the brewing guide.

screenshots.caption: Maya's paused goal shows two work sessions, updated planning for eight people and a next step awaiting final approval.
notes: This is actual saved goal progress. The original goal description still mentions six adults, while the later progress summary describes eight. A task card below also shows the updated venue and date.

screenshots.caption: Maya's final response includes a 90-minute run sheet from 10:00 to 11:30 with a decaf handling note.
notes: Later capture of the persisted real chat output. Conversation completed is a chat status; the assistant's claim that all tasks are complete is not alone proof of goal-controller completion. See 16-day3-goal-completed.png for the actual saved goal status.

screenshots.caption: Operator-reviewed final workshop details and quantities are saved as Important memory.
notes: The agent operating the software corrected this memory and marked it important. The visible owner-approval wording records the demonstration's approval step; it is not independent human acceptance. Planning quantities are distinguished from the source's brewing instructions.

screenshots.caption: The saved goal is marked Goal completed after four work sessions, with completed shopping, run-sheet and invitation tasks visible.
notes: Actual controller completion is visible. The root goal's old description still mentions six adults and its stale Next step still asks for final approval, although the completion summary records eight adults and fulfilled approval. The shopping task shows the corrected final quantities. The fourth child task is outside this frame.

installationEvidence.reason: The initial installation happened before the main screen recording.
installationEvidence.precondition: The task-owned installation prefix did not exist before this take.
installationEvidence.reused: Existing Node/npm tooling and npm download cache; this was a new package prefix and fresh app data, not a fresh machine.
installationEvidence.launch: An initial launch on port 4201 failed with EADDRINUSE because the main runtime's sidecar occupied it. The fresh-data instance then started on port 4300 and returned HTTP 200.
installationEvidence.receipt: 00-install-receipt.png re-displays the actual npm installation log, npm ls result and ready URL after the command completed. It is a real terminal receipt view, not the original in-progress command frame.
installationEvidence.limits: The measured installation used cached downloads and excludes the initial machine setup. It is not a first-install time estimate.
